subject: Discovery summary: Observability + Evals pilot for Skyline AI
messages:
Date: 2026-03-20T15:02:00-07:00
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@skyline.ai>, Maria Chen <maria@skyline.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today's observability + evals discovery

Hi Alex / Maria —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discussion and the next steps we proposed so your team can align internally.

Pain points you described
- Invisible model regressions in production — you only discover issues via support tickets (hours → days).
- No standard golden prompt set for regression testing across releases; QA runs are manual and brittle.
- Limited tracing into prompt/response lifecycle (hard to map downstream app errors back to model outputs).
- Cost unpredictability when spikes occur; difficulty correlating cost to specific routes.

Current stack
- App: Node.js microservices on AWS Fargate
- Models: self-hosted Llama variants behind a basic proxy
- Observability: Datadog for infra; limited model telemetry (logs only)
- CI: GitHub Actions; no formal eval CI gate yet

Success criteria you shared
1) Alerting on regressions within 15 minutes of occurrence (actionable signal).
2) Per-route token cost and latency visibility to keep <250ms p50 for core flows.
3) Automated golden-prompt regression tests in CI with pass/fail reporting.
4) Safe rollout guardrails so a bad model can be automatically rolled back.

What Redwood can deliver (high level)
- Redwood Console dashboards: per-route cost, latency percentiles, and token breakdowns.
- Tracing hooks: request-level IDs that persist across your proxy → Redwood so you can join logs in Datadog.
- Evals integration: golden-prompt sets stored in GDrive, CI-run evals with regression alerts (Slack/PagerDuty).
- Rollout policies: canary + automatic fallback to a pinned model variant on quality regression.

Agreed next steps
1) We will share the golden-prompts template and a sample dashboard this week (attachment + Drive link). — Dev
2) Marcus to spin up a short demo of Console tracing and rollback on Tue 2026-03-23 11:00 PT — Marcus
3) Alex to share a copy of one failing support ticket and the token cost for the route (for tuning batching) — Alex
4) Security questionnaire: Laura will follow up with the SOC2/infra items if we proceed to a Duo/SOC2 review — Laura

Attachments: redwood-observability-plan.pdf (example layouts), golden-prompts-template.csv (format for CI).

Thanks again — I'll follow up with the Drive links and a calendar invite for Marcus' demo.

Best,
Dev Patel

Thanks Dev — this is great, aligns with what we heard internally. Couple clarifications:
- The regression alerts should be actionable: ideally include a top-3 failing prompts and a link to the failing request for triage.
- For rollout guardrails, we need percent-of-traffic thresholds and an ability to pause and rollback automatically if eval scores drop below a threshold.

I'll upload a redacted support ticket and token-export by EOD Monday. Also, FYI, our SRE wants a Datadog-compatible trace ID header rather than a separate console-only ID.

See you on Tue for the demo — Marcus, please make sure we see the trace join and the automatic rollback in action.
